consumer:sa.personal_property_tax_any@i1.question_phrase: charged every year and based on the value of the property

consumer:sa.medical_premiums@i1040sca:p1.question_phrase: pay for health insurance with money that had already been taxed

consumer:sa.mortgage_unreported@i1040sca.question_phrase: pay home mortgage interest or points in 2025 that are not reported to you on Form 1098

consumer:sc.employees@i1040sc:p7.question_phrase: Did this business have employees in 2025?

consumer:sc.employees@i1040sc:p8.question_phrase: Did this business have employees in 2025?

consumer:sc.travel_meals@i1040sc:p9.source_phrase: connected with overnight travel for business while away from your tax home

consumer:sc.travel_meals@p587:p13.source_phrase: You can deduct as a business expense 100% of the actual cost of food consumed by your daycare recipients
consumer:sc.travel_meals@p587:p13.reason: Food for daycare recipients is food the business paid for, which the question asks (its help names daycare food), so a provider with the page's 100% deduction answers Yes.

consumer:sc.goods@f1040sc:p2.source_phrase: Purchases less cost of items withdrawn for personal use

consumer:f2441.benefits@i2441:p5.source_phrase: include amounts you received under a dependent care assistance program from your sole proprietorship or partnership

consumer:scope.care_benefits_other@i2441.question_phrase: for example from your own business or a partnership), or carried into 2025 from a 2024 plan under a grace period

consumer:scope.cfc@i1040gi:p91.source_phrase: Section 951 generally requires that a U.S. shareholder of a controlled foreign corporation include in income its pro rata share
consumer:scope.cfc@i1040gi:p91.reason: The question names the controlled foreign corporation of lines 8n and 8o and describes it more widely (any U.S. owners, not only 10% shareholders), which only refuses more returns.

consumer:scope.foreign_shares@i1040gi:p9.question_phrase: own shares of a company or a fund set up outside the United States, other than through a U.S. mutual fund or ETF

consumer:scope.clergy@i1040sse:p1.question_phrase: as a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, or as a Christian Science practitioner
consumer:scope.clergy@i1040sse:p1.source_phrase: Ministers, Members of Religious Orders, and Christian Science Practitioners

consumer:scope.excess_deferral@i1040gi:p.question_phrase: put more of your pay into retirement plans at work than the yearly limit

consumer:scope.f8615@i8615:p1.question_phrase: was a parent of yours alive, and were you either under 18, or 18 (or a full-time student aged 19 to 23) with pay for work of no more than half of what it cost to support you

consumer:scope.armed_forces@i1040gi:p93.reason: Reserve and National Guard members and active-duty members moving under orders (the page's line 12 and line 14 cases) served in 2025 and answer Yes for either spouse.

consumer:scope.reservist_expenses@i1040g.question_phrase: deduct costs, not paid back, of travel more than 100 miles from home for reserve or National Guard duty in 2025
consumer:scope.reservist_expenses@i1040g.source_phrase: Certain business expenses of National Guard and reserve members who traveled more than 100 miles from home

consumer:scope.armed_forces@i1040gi:p95.source_phrase: Don’t include any repayments of qualified reservist distributions.

consumer:scope.noncitizen@i1040gi:p8.question_phrase: At any time in 2025, were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) not a U.S. citizen?

consumer:scope.nonresident@i1040gi:p8.question_phrase: For any part of 2025, were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) a nonresident alien
consumer:scope.nonresident@i1040gi:p8.source_phrase: Most nonresident aliens and dual-status aliens have different filing requirements
consumer:scope.nonresident@i1040gi:p8.reason: Nonresidence for any part of the year covers both of the page's groups, nonresident and dual-status aliens, for either spouse, and a Yes refuses.

consumer:scope.performer_expenses@i1040g.question_phrase: deduct costs for that work, not paid back, under the rules for a 'qualified performing artist' or an official paid by fees

consumer:scope.f8978@i1040gi:p34.source_phrase: Tax from Form 8978, line 14 (relating to partner’s audit liability under section 6226)

consumer:scope.pfic@i1040gi:p114.source_phrase: Enter any interest amount from Form 8621, line 16f, relating to distributions from, and dispositions of, stock of a section 1291 fund

consumer:scope.pfic@i1040gi:p34.question_phrase: a fund, or a company whose income or assets are mostly investments, set up outside the United States (a 'passive foreign investment company')
